title: The Teams app stays on the sign-in screen on one laptop
scenario: A single accounting laptop has lost its primary refresh token after a stale device registration; the browser works, a cache clear does not help, and re-registering the device fixes it.

events.title: Cannot use Teams app on my laptop
events.text: Hi, I'm Ines from accounting. Since Monday my laptop will not let me into the Teams app. It keeps asking for my password and then says something went wrong. A colleague two desks away has no problem at all. Nobody told me about any change.

events.title: Re: Cannot use Teams app on my laptop
events.text: Hello Ines, sorry about that. Can you check whether Teams in a web browser lets you in with the same account? And please clear the Teams cache: close Teams, delete the Teams folder under your AppData, and start it again.

events.title: Re: Cannot use Teams app on my laptop
events.text: The browser works, I am in with the same account. I cleared the cache like you said and it still fails the same way in the app.

events.title: Re: Cannot use Teams app on my laptop
events.text: Thanks. Since only the desktop app on your laptop fails, I would like to look at the device itself. Please open a command prompt, run dsregcmd /status and paste the part called SSO State (it shows a line AzureAdPrt). If your colleague whose Teams works can run it too, we can compare the two.

events.title: Re: Cannot use Teams app on my laptop
events.text: Here it is. Mine: AzureAdPrt: NO, AzureAdPrtUpdateTime 2026-06-12 07:44:10 UTC. Marta's laptop two desks away: AzureAdPrt: YES, updated this morning.

events.title: Sign-in logs for ines.f
events.text: No failed sign-in rows at all for ines.f in today's logs, although she has tried many times. The failures happen on the laptop before anything is sent to the service.

events.title: What I think it is
events.text: This fits a laptop that has lost its primary refresh token: AzureAdPrt is NO on yours and YES on your colleague's, and the logs are clean. It often follows a stale device registration. Please sign out of Windows, restart, sign in on the office network and run dsregcmd /status once more. If it still says NO, your IT admin should run dsregcmd /leave from an admin prompt, restart, and let the laptop register again with your work account.

events.title: Re: What I think it is
events.text: I did the first part and it still says NO. Our IT admin is doing the leave and register now, he is connected to my laptop.

events.title: Re: What I think it is
events.text: It worked! After the new registration it shows AzureAdPrt: YES and Teams opened at once. Thank you!

events.title: Closing note
events.text: Re-registered laptop shows AzureAdPrt YES, the Teams desktop app signs in, the user confirmed. Cause: a stale device registration on this laptop. Their IT admin will check the other laptops from the same batch.
